messages:
elaine: Customer (Acme Corp) opened a severity-2 ticket — they see intermittent 502s from our hosted API when doing long streaming requests / large payloads. Started ~2026-03-16 18:10 UTC. Repro steps they gave:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream" -d '{\"prompt\": \"...huge payload...\"}'

They see the stream drop after a few minutes with 502, and they have trace ids: trace=acme-01-8f3a, trace=acme-01-8f3b. Asking oncall for immediate triage and any mitigations we can offer the customer.

dan: Looking. Do we know if this is authenticated (their hosted key) or guest traffic? Also can you paste one of the trace ids as a full X-Request-Id header so I can find logs?

elaine: Authenticated (hosted key). One full header from their call: X-Request-Id: acme-01-8f3a, X-Redwood-Trace: acme-01-8f3a. Customer says it only happens for very long-lived HTTP/2 streams (streaming inference), not short requests.

priya: I'm seeing a matching spike on ingress -> envoy.upstream_rq_5xx around 18:09-18:14 UTC for that pool. Also envoys are logging upstream resets with RST_STREAM/CANCEL. Quick grep from ingress pod: 

```
2026-03-16T18:10:11.234Z envoy info [12345] stream 0x7f2e: reply error: upstream reset: connection failure, error code 1 (RST_STREAM)
2026-03-16T18:10:11.235Z envoy warn cluster ingress-backends: cluster max connections reached, dropping new stream
```
I also see kernel backlog drops on the node (accept queue full) around same time: `netstat -s` shows SYN cookies incrementing on those nodes.

mike: That looks like socket/accept queue saturation rather than application-level CPU. Long-lived HTTP/2 streams keep connections busy and can starve the accept/dispatch path when a few clients open many parallel streams. Kernel then starts dropping/queueing and envoy reports connection overflow -> 502 for new streams.

Quick mitigations we can try (fast):
- Temporarily throttle that customer's concurrency from the API side (rate-limit by API key)
- Bump node accept backlog (sysctl net.core.somaxconn) on ingress nodes and restart envoy (can be rollout)
- Lower http2_max_concurrent_streams in envoy cluster so a single connection can't hog too many streams

I can patch a canary with a lowered `http2_max_concurrent_streams: 128` and `circuit_breakers.max_connections` bump on one ingress AZ.

dan: +1 to canary. Also we should capture pcap/sniffer on one affected node to confirm accept queue saturation. For quick customer-facing mitigation, throttle them to 8 concurrent streams and request they retry with exponential backoff — that'll stop immediate 502 surface area.

elaine: I told the customer to reduce concurrency and add retries. They pushed back but accepted a temporary throttle while we investigate.

priya: I've deployed the canary with lowered http2_max_concurrent_streams on ingress-canary (AZ-a). Envoy logs show reduced RST_STREAMs from that pod. Metrics: upstream_cx_overflow dropped from 420 -> 30 in the canary after the change.

mike: I'll schedule a safe node sysctl bump across ingress fleet and then increase somaxconn from 128 -> 1024; will coordinate a rolling restart of envoy to pick up settings. Also propose we add a connection backlog metric and an alert so we detect this earlier.

dan: Follow-up items:
- infra: node somaxconn bump + rolling restart (mike)
- oncall: monitor canary impact / rollback if errors increase (priya)
- support: confirm customer behavior and remove throttle when stable (elaine)
- eng-runtime: investigate whether we should gate very large streaming payloads with token-bucket at routing layer (dan)

elaine: Customer reports errors dropped dramatically after we throttled them and canary is healthy. I'll update the ticket and schedule a postmortem with Acme for next week. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy record — ingress-canary updated http2_max_concurrent_streams=128 by priya at 2026-03-16T19:05:23Z

elaine: Closing loop in ticket with steps we took and recommended long-term fixes.
